subject: Redwood POC: setup blockers and proposed next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@atlaspay.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@atlaspay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T15:10:00Z
Subject: Redwood POC: initial sync + recommended next steps

Thanks again for the call today — appreciated the walkthrough of AtlasPay's fraud-review flow and the volume profile. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single place to track: 

- Goal: validate 95th-percentile latency under production-like load and measure token-cost impact for our reranking use-case.
- Resources I shared: onboarding runbook (link below), minimal test harness, and a sandbox model snapshot we can pin to the POC.
- Immediate blockers you mentioned: network egress policy and an internal approval for third-party env access.

Proposed next steps:
1) Add our engineer to your VPC contacts so we can validate firewall rules (suggested: staging subnet access to port 443).
2) Share a short list of three sample requests (anonymized) we can use to get initial telemetry.
3) Book a 60-min remote pairing session next week to walk through agent setup and confirm the KV cache behavior.

I attached the onboarding runbook with the setup checklist and a brief troubleshooting section. If it's helpful, Marissa from Solutions can lead the pairing session — she has a concise step checklist we can follow.

Thanks — will wait for a quick note on availability.

Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-onboarding-runbook.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@atlaspay.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T09:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Redwood POC: initial sync + recommended next steps

Thanks Karthik — useful summary. Two quick updates from our side: 

- Liam will own the VPC network work; he expects to need a short IP allowlist and a signed non-prod access agreement from our security team.
- We've pulled together the sample payloads but need to scrub PII before we share.

I expect the security approval to be the longer pole here (1–2 weeks). We'll prioritize the allowlist so you can at least run smoke checks. Can you send a dedicated IP range and the exact ports to open?

Best,
Sophie
Product Manager, AtlasPay

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@atlaspay.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@atlaspay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Redwood POC: initial sync + recommended next steps

Appreciate the update Sophie — attaching a short network requirements worksheet + the specific egress IPs you'll see traffic from. If your security team would prefer a temporary SSH tunnel relay instead of an IP allowlist for the initial pairing, we can support that as well to avoid formal firewall changes during the first smoke tests.

Attachment: atlas-network-requirements.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Marissa — looping you in to coordinate the pairing session. Can you propose two 60-min slots next week (PST morning / EST afternoon) so AtlasPay can pick?

Karthik

To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@atlaspay.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@atlaspay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T09:15:00Z
Subject: Quick pulse — looks like onboarding hasn't started in the console

Sophie / Liam — checking in following up on the network worksheet I sent last week. I pulled the POC tenant for AtlasPay and I'm not seeing any connection attempts in the first-stage telemetry.

If security approval is the blocker, two low-effort options that other customers have used:
- Temporary reverse-proxy / SSH relay (no change to corporate firewall rules)
- Short-term client cert pinning to an allowlisted proxy IP we provide

If neither of those are workable, we can also run a scoped, turnkey test where Redwood ingests an anonymized batch you drop into a secure S3 share and we run the smoke checks on your behalf. That avoids any network changes on your side but still gives you the latency/cost numbers.

Can you share which option would be easiest and a rough ETA? If it's lower priority for the month, a quick "pause" note is totally fine — just trying to avoid building scheduling friction later.

Thanks,
Karthik

Hi Sophie / Liam — Ben from Customer Success here, stepping in to make this frictionless. Karthik flagged that telemetry hasn't started; we can either: 

A) Run a 45-min hands-on onboarding session this week (we'll do the tunnel if you prefer no firewall change).
B) Accept a secure S3 drop of anonymized payloads and run the smoke tests ourselves (we'll deliver a short report and the latency/cost breakdown).

If you have an existing security reviewer who needs to see an IP and cert summary, I can send a short one-page security brief that our SOC team signs off on — we've used it for customers with strict internal vendors.

Proposed times for a live session: Thu 2026-11-18 09:00–09:45 PST or Fri 2026-11-19 13:00–13:45 PST. If those don't work, drop 1–2 slots that do and we'll lock it.

Thanks — happy to be pragmatic here.

Ben Carter
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
